record.hypothesis: For all four datasets, add a fixed frequency-derived input scale computed solely from training item counts: normalize log1p(count)^(-0.25) to mean one and clip to [0.75, 1.25]. Multiply observed-item input embeddings by this scale; leave padding, mask tokens and candidate embeddings unchanged. This may reduce domination by frequent context items while preserving embedding parameters, BERT topology, readout, loss and optimizer. Store the scales with each category checkpoint and apply identically in the predictor writer.

category_rationales.rationale: Scale observed context embeddings using training-only item frequencies to reduce frequent-item dominance. Normalize inverse-quarter-power log counts to mean one, then clip to [0.75, 1.25]. Padding, mask tokens, unseen items and candidate embeddings retain unit scale. A persistent buffer saves the feature with each checkpoint; the generated predictor imports the same model class and restores it automatically. Learned embeddings, topology, readout, loss and optimizer remain fixed.
